references.text: The preceding verse explains why Aaron and the leaders had withdrawn – they were afraid to approach Moses because of the light that shone from his face.
Aaron and the leaders of the congregation (נְשִׂיאִים) are mentioned together as representatives of the people, in the same way as in this text.
Describes the chiefs of the congregation (נְשִׂיאִים), the same leaders who returned to Moses together with Aaron.
The chiefs of Israel (נְשִׂיאִים), who were heads of their ancestral houses, correspond to the leaders whom Moses called to him.
The following verse continues the narrative and tells what Moses said to them – he gave them all the commands the Lord had spoken to him on Mount Sinai.
Paul refers to Moses' radiant face and how he spoke to the children of Israel, using this as an image of the glory of the old covenant compared with the glory of the new covenant.
Both illustrate Moses' role as a gatherer of leadership to convey God's will at critical turning points.
Parallel structure for 'going out' from God's presence: Lev 9 shows blessing and glory, Ex 34 shows restoration of fellowship.
Both describe Moses' initiative to gather Aaron and the leaders for a decisive worship or covenant event.
Theological contrast between the beginning of deliverance (Ex 4) and the restoration of leadership after sin (Ex 34).
Complementary aspects of God's holiness: Lev 10 shows judgment over unclean approach, Ex 34 shows restoration of a close relationship.
Clear contrast: Ex 34 shows the leaders' obedient restoration, while Num 16 shows rebellion against the same authority.
